text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in today's Russian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- Trans-World Group, the UK-based commodities powerhouse, is planning to bid for 38 percent of Russia's mining giant Norilsk Nickel.
- Russia's Finance Ministry intends to establish control over Russia's gold market by intruducing some new rules in trading gold.
- Despite obvious opposition in the defence ministry, sweeping changes will be launched in the army, says Defence Minister Igor Sergeyev.
- The president of the southeastern Kalmyk republic, Kirsan Ilyumzhinov, says he is Russia's richest official, announcing his income last year of almost six billion roubles (one million dollars).
SEVODNYA
- Moscow's international airport has opened another runaway, promising to end delays of landings and takeoffs of all types of aircrafts in all weather conditions.

- Russia's government, after receiving the right to take the decisions itself, will work out a new list of companies for auctioning, the paper quotes First Deputy Finance Minister Alexei Kudrin as saying.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA

- A new bill "On Freedom of Conscience and Religion", to be either approved or vetoed by Boris Yeltsin, has become a subject of political trading after the U.S Senate and the Vatican expressed concern over the document.
- Russia's Security Council will have to discuss the growing tension between the ethnic minorities of the two Caucasian republics bordering Chechnya.
- The situation in the army is under control, says the head of the military counter-intelligence service.
IZVESTIA

- A meeting of officials at Mission Control on Monday may decide to force the present crew to abandon plans to make repair power cables in the airless Spektr module and may put in doubt French scientist Leopold Eyharts' planned participation in a mission scheduled to start on August 5, taking a relief crew to Mir.
- Seventy-six people have been kidnapped in Chechnya in the last six months, according to local Interior Ministry statistics.
ROSSIISKAYA GAZETA

- President Boris Yeltsin has ordered the defence ministry to cut troop numbers by 500,000 to 1.2 million by the end of the next year in a series of measures intended to turn the Russian army into a more effective fighting force.
ROSSIISKIYE VESTI

- A controversial bill "On Freedom of Conscience and Religious Association", aimed at curbing the rights of minority religions, is said to be premature and counter-productive but is needed very much, says the official presidential paper.
- The space station Mir is old, but there is nothing to replace it with and it will orbit the Earth till 2000 at least.
- Tatyana Ustinova, Moscow newsroom, +7095 941 8520.
